text:
alex: quick question — before we flip the econ console rollout I want to confirm how we show prefetch vs hotpath costs. current PR adds a single "prefetch_adjusted_tokens" column which folds credits into the per-invocation token count. i'm worried that will confuse product and SRE who expect raw token burn + separate credit line.

hannah: +1 that was my worry too. can we show both? raw_tokens, prefetch_credits, net_tokens. small columns, tooltip explaining how credits are attributed. :information_source:

miguel: from telemetry side we only have deterministic raw token counts. prefetch credits are derived later in the pipeline (batch-level amortization). showing both requires a join to the cache-attribution table which is sampled at 1% today.

alex: do we have an estimate of how noisy net_tokens will be at 1% sampling? if it swings +/- 10% that's probably fine but if it's +/-50% it will be misleading.

miguel: quick calc: for tenants with >10k invocations/day sampling variance is ~3-5% on net tokens. below that it's noisy. we could add a confidence badge.

rachel: UX asks: would product prefer a switch to "show estimated net cost" vs "show raw burn"? toggle in header, default to raw for first rollout. also request a sparkline of net vs raw over 7d.

alex: toggle sounds safe. also need to reconcile quota math: if we display net_tokens users may think quotas consumed are net, but quota enforcement uses raw tokens.
hannah: we should annotate quota column with "enforced on raw tokens" and a hover explainer. Tom from billing asked for an export that has both columns for reconciliation.

miguel: implementation notes: pipeline change to backfill prefetch attribution join for last 90 days will take ~2h compute for full window. live queries should use a new precomputed view: econ.view_prefetch_credits_v1. i'll add it to the PR.

infra-bot: deploy-stage:cost-db-migrations queued (runbook #314). ETA ~45m.

alex: thanks. one more API debate — internal telemetry REST endpoint /v1/econ/summary currently returns raw_tokens and samples_percent. do we expand it to include prefetch_credits and confidence_interval? that'll break one internal consumer (ops-alerts).

sam: ops-alerts can tolerate a new optional field if we keep backward-compatible keys. add prefetch_credits as nullable with sample_rate metadata.

hannah: also propose adding a per-tenant flag in the UI to hide net estimate when sample_rate < 5%. fewer confused users.

rachel: For rollout plan: canary to 5 teams (internal + 4 customers), monitor: net_vs_raw_ratio, tickets mentioning 'billing' in first 24h, query latency for econ endpoint. if all good, scale to org-wide.

alex: agreed. action items: (1) miguel to create view_prefetch_credits_v1 + backfill job, (2) rachel to add toggle + confidence badge UX, (3) sam to add optional fields to /v1/econ/summary, (4) hannah to draft tooltip copy and quota annotation. i'll own the canary and communicate to billing.

miguel: ETA for view + backfill: EOD tomorrow if nothing blocks.

sam: I'll add schema patch to the internal swagger and create a feature flag for the optional fields.

hannah: I'll draft copy and send to legal/billing for a quick sanity check.

alex: awesome. leaving this thread here, ping me if you need signoff to flip the canary. :thumbsup:
